## Dataset & Null Hypothesis Sampling Distribution

You'll work with a dataset called `cpr` about patients who had heart attacks, were given CPR, and then were admitted to the hospital. Once in the hospital, they were either given blood thinners (`treatment` group) or not (`control` group). The experiment then measured whether they survived at least 24 hours.

Run the code below to see a random 10 rows of the dataset.
```{code-blanks}
slice_sample(cpr, n = 10)
```

Answer Questions 5-10 of your packet, then **stop** and check in with Dr. O or Aidan.

Then use those responses to fill in this code to generate your null hypothesis sampling distribution (or "null distribution" for short).

```{code-blanks}
#| blank:
#|   target: outcome
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: group
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: survived
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: "diff in props"
#|   prefill: true
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: treatment
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: control
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token

null_dist <- cpr |>
  specify(response = outcome, explanatory = group, success = "survived") |>
  hypothesize(null = "independence") |>
  generate(reps = 5000, type = "permute") |>
  calculate(stat = "diff in props", order = c("treatment","control"))

visualize(null_dist)

```

Answer Question 11 in the packet.

## Finding the p-value

Answer Question 16 in your packet, then fill in the code below to answer Question 17.

```{code-blanks}
#| blank:

#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: sample_stat
#|   prefill: true
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token

null_dist |>
  visualize() + 
  shade_p_value(sample_stat, direction = "right")

```
